title: BEA Benchmark Input-Output Accounts Timeline (Phase-0 canonical reference)
scope: US Bureau of Economic Analysis benchmark input-output (I-O) accounts: benchmark years, classification system (SIC vs NAICS), industry-detail/order, and the capital-flow benchmark matrix, as relevant to the RSCD replication of Shaikh (2016) Chapters 6/7/9.
benchmark_cadence: BEA publishes a benchmark I-O account every 5 years, for years ending in 2 and 7, keyed to the quinquennial Economic Census.
detail_levels: Benchmark I-O is generally available at four levels: sector (~15 industry groups), summary (~71 groups), underlying summary (~138 groups), and detail (~402-405 industries). Detail-level estimates are available only for benchmark years.

cross_checks.local_CH9_RESEARCH_SUMMARY: Confirms Shaikh's 1947-1998 I-O panel uses six benchmark cross-sections (1947,1958,1963,1967,1972,1998); 1947-1972 from Ochoa (1984) 71-order; 1998 from BEA industry-by-industry Use table 65-order; NAICS-vs-SIC break prevents a continuous panel; capital-flow benchmark matrix unavailable post-1997.
cross_checks.local_ADR-005_NAICS: Local naics_concordance_master.csv already stages NAICS 2002-2022 stability flags for Shaikh's 30-industry Ch7 sample. This timeline adds the upstream benchmark-year classification history and the official Census concordance files.

benchmark_years.notable_change: First BEA benchmark I-O. Basis for Shaikh/Ochoa 1947 71-order cross-section.
Shaikh/Ochoa 1972 cross-section (last of the historical Ochoa 71-order panel used by Shaikh).
Not used in Shaikh's Ch9 panel (his historical set jumps 1972 -> 1998).
Last-but-one SIC benchmark; anchors the 1987-SIC side of the Census SIC<->NAICS bridge.
LAST SIC-basis benchmark I-O. Do not splice to 1997+ (classification break).

FIRST NAICS-basis benchmark I-O. Hard classification break vs. 1992-and-earlier SIC benchmarks. First benchmark to include software as investment. Also the LAST benchmark capital-flow table (see capital_flow_matrix).
Incorporated into the 2009 NIPA comprehensive revision. Published SCB Oct 2007.
First benchmark FULLY INTEGRATED with the annual industry accounts and the NIPAs (supply-use framework). Incorporated into the 2013 NIPA comprehensive revision.
Incorporated into the 2018 NIPA comprehensive update. 2007<->2012 I-O concordance in SCB Aug 2018 Appendix A.
Incorporated into the 2023 harmonized comprehensive update; 2017-NAICS effects small (no summary/sector reclassifications). Most recent benchmark as of 2026-06-30.

classification_break.impact: The 1947-1992 benchmark I-O tables are SIC-based; the 1997+ tables are NAICS-based. BEA states the historical (pre-1997) tables 'should not be used as a time series' and do not reflect subsequent NIPA comprehensive revisions. For RSCD Ch9 this is the hard limit that prevents splicing the Ochoa 1947-1972 71-order panel to the 1998 BEA 65-order NAICS Use table into one continuous series.

industry_order_notes.detail: Shaikh's Ch9 historical cross-sections (1947,1958,1963,1967,1972) reuse Ochoa (1984)'s 71-industry-order compilation (as in Shaikh 1998a); real estate is excluded from the Ochoa tables. Shaikh's 1998 cross-section uses BEA's 65-order industry-by-industry Use table (post-redefinition), with the real-estate column corrected for owner-occupied-housing imputations (NIPA T7.12 lines 133-134). The 71-order and 65-order schemes are not directly conformable.

BEA benchmark summary detail is ~71 industry groups; underlying-summary ~138; detail ~402-405 (2007+). The 'order' (row/column sequence and aggregation) is revised at each benchmark, so industry indices are not stable across benchmark years even within the NAICS era.

capital_flow_matrix.description: The BEA benchmark CAPITAL FLOW TABLE (capital flow matrix): a use-type-by-using-industry matrix distributing new equipment, software, and structures investment across using industries.
capital_flow_matrix.cadence: Historically produced for each benchmark year (years ending in 2 and 7).
capital_flow_matrix.release: 1997 capital flow table released in SCB November 2003; it was the seventh in the series and the FIRST on a NAICS basis and the first to include software as an investment category.
capital_flow_matrix.discontinuation: No benchmark capital-flow table has been published for 2002 or later; the benchmark capital-flow matrix was effectively DISCONTINUED after 1997. (BEA later explored ANNUAL capital-flow tables as research, but the fixed benchmark asset-by-industry matrix ends at 1997.)
capital_flow_matrix.rscd_impact: Shaikh's Ch9 fixed-capital wage-profit model distributes BEA Fixed Asset Tables 3.1ES/3.4ES across industries USING the 1997 benchmark capital flow matrix. Any post-1998 fixed-capital replication must APPROXIMATE the asset-by-industry distribution from BEA's detailed Fixed Asset Tables (by type x industry) because the benchmark matrix no longer exists. This is CH9 open-question 4 and a structural obstacle to extension.
